clinician.trajectory_summary: A 61-year-old woman with no significant past medical history presented to the ED with a 1-week fever associated with progressive headache, bilateral leg weakness, and paresthesias. Physical examination revealed slight neck stiffness with otherwise normal vital parameters. Lumbar puncture demonstrated moderate pleocytosis (140 leucocytes/μL with mononuclear cell dominance) and mild inflammatory syndrome, consistent with viral meningoencephalitis. CT scan of the brain was normal. MRI revealed characteristic findings of TBEV encephalitis: T2-weighted hyperintense signal in the tegmentum pontis and cerebellar vermis, with FLAIR sequence showing hyperintensity and swelling of the entire cerebellar vermis with minimal paravermis involvement and sparing of the cerebellar hemispheres. These imaging findings, combined with the clinical presentation (fever, headache, meningeal signs, neurological symptoms) and CSF pleocytosis with lymphocytic predominance, are pathognomonic for TBEV encephalitis.

CSF pleocytosis with lymphocytic predominance (140 leucocytes/μL with mononuclear cell dominance) indicating viral meningoencephalitis
Mild inflammatory syndrome on laboratory findings
Normal CT scan ruling out acute structural lesions or hemorrhage
MRI showing characteristic T2-weighted hyperintense signal in tegmentum pontis and cerebellar vermis—classic pattern for TBEV encephalitis
MRI FLAIR sequence showing hyperintensity and swelling of cerebellar vermis with minimal paravermis involvement and sparing of cerebellar hemispheres—pathognomonic for TBEV
